item.text:
**7B.1 Research Note: Narendra Modi in 2024**

**Bottom line**
The record is mixed but leans negative. There is some evidence Modi told the truth in high-stakes diplomatic settings and accepted the election result procedurally. But the stronger 2024 pattern is recurring evasive or misleading public messaging, especially on communal politics, plus state-backed information control and attacks on scrutiny. I did not find strong independent evidence of routine candor to courts or legislature in the indexed 2024 material.

**Accepted Claims**
- **Accepted coalition rule after electoral setback** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 4 Jun 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-set-to-win-historic-third-term-but-with-surprisingly-slim-majority/2116973/ | Summary: Reuters reported that the BJP fell short of a solo majority and Modi framed the result as a coalition mandate. This is positive procedural evidence that he did not deny the electoral outcome, though it is about accepting power constraints rather than broad truthfulness. | Question IDs: 7B.1, 6B.9, 6B.10
- **Took office normally after the setback** | Publisher: Prime Minister’s Office / PIB | Date: 9 Jun 2024 | URL: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2023675&lang=2&reg=48 | Summary: The oath-taking record shows a regular constitutional transfer of office. This supports limited truthfulness/procedural honesty in dealing with the electorate and constitutional system, but it does not by itself show habitual candor. | Question IDs: 7B.1, 6B.9, 6B.10
- **Public denial of anti-Muslim intent after divisive campaign rhetoric** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 7 May 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/indian-pm-modi-says-he-does-not-oppose-islam-muslims-as-election-campaign-heats-up/2072917/ | Summary: Modi denied opposing Muslims after criticism over “infiltrators” rhetoric. This is relevant because it is a self-defense statement against an allegation that would damage reputation; the denial is counterevidence only if one accepts the surrounding reporting as more credible. | Question IDs: 7B.1, 6B.8, 6B.10
- **Campaign rhetoric linked Muslims to a false redistribution narrative** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 22 Apr 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/indias-congress-seeks-action-against-modi-for-comments-about-muslims/2051980/ | Summary: Reuters reported that Modi said Congress wanted to redistribute Hindu wealth to Muslims and referred to Muslims as “infiltrators.” That is strong evidence of misleading or deceptive political messaging designed to protect power by inflaming fear. | Question IDs: 7B.1, 6B.8, 6B.10
- **Shifted from development talk to communal attack messaging** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 23 Apr 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-calls-rivals-pro-muslim-as-election-campaign-changes-tack/2053223/ | Summary: Reuters described Modi pivoting away from development messaging toward anti-Muslim attacks and wealth-redistribution warnings. This is negative evidence for truthfulness because it suggests strategic distortion of public debate for electoral gain. | Question IDs: 7B.1, 6B.8, 6B.10
- **Election Commission censure over divisive speech** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 22 May 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/indias-poll-panel-orders-modis-bjp-opposition-congress-to-show-restraint-in-campaign/2096809/ | Summary: The EC told BJP campaigners to stop communal campaigning after complaints about divisive speech, including Modi’s remarks. Formal censure is strong counterevidence to a habit of telling the truth when false or inflammatory claims would help politically. | Question IDs: 7B.1, 6B.8, 6B.10
- **BJP campaign videos promoted enmity** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 6 May 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/india-bjps-election-videos-targeting-muslims-and-opposition-spark-outrage/2072180/ | Summary: Reuters reported campaign videos targeting Muslims and opposition parties, with complaints that they promoted enmity and provoked rioting. This supports a finding of willingness to use deceptive or inflammatory messaging rather than straightforward truth-telling. | Question IDs: 7B.1, 6B.8
- **Fact-check unit attempted state information control** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 21 Mar 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/india-top-court-puts-on-hold-unit-for-fact-checking-online-content-about-govt/2009612/ | Summary: The government created a fact-checking unit with power to flag content about government business as false or misleading; the Supreme Court stayed it. This does not prove Modi lied, but it is strong evidence that the administration was willing to control truth claims about itself when that protected power. | Question IDs: 7B.1, 6B.9, 6B.8
- **Pressure on the independent press and foreign correspondents** | Publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | Date: 13 Nov 2024 | URL: https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/news/inside-modis-crackdown-foreign-press-india | Summary: The Reuters Institute reported visa and work-permit denials and pressure on foreign correspondents critical of the government. That is indirect but meaningful evidence against a truth-telling habit, because governments that are comfortable with the truth rarely need to intimidate the messengers. | Question IDs: 7B.1, 6B.9, 6B.8
- **Press freedom concerns and regulatory pressure** | Publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | Date: 17 Jun 2024 | URL: https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/india | Summary: Reuters Institute noted new laws, broad regulatory powers, and the NewsClick raids as chilling press freedom. This is negative background evidence for truthfulness because it points to an environment where embarrassing facts were harder to surface. | Question IDs: 7B.1, 6B.9, 6B.8
- **Straightforward civilian-protection message to Putin** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 9 Jul 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/modi-tells-putin-that-death-of-innocent-children-is-very-painful/2167042/ | Summary: Modi told Putin that the death of innocent children is painful and that the Ukraine war could not be solved on the battlefield. This is one of the best positive items for truthfulness to an international partner in a live crisis, because it is direct, non-evasive, and publicly consistent with India’s peace line. | Question IDs: 7B.1, 1B.4, 6B.6
- **Publicly repeated diplomacy-and-dialogue line on Ukraine** | Publisher: Prime Minister’s Office / PIB | Date: 24 Sep 2024 | URL: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2058086&lang=2&reg=48 | Summary: Modi reiterated a “clear, consistent and constructive approach” favoring diplomacy and dialogue and said India remained open to a lasting settlement. This is positive evidence that he was at least candid and consistent with an international partner on a major war issue. | Question IDs: 7B.1, 1B.4, 6B.6
- **Strong anti-escalatory Quad statement** | Publisher: Prime Minister’s Office / PIB | Date: 22 Sep 2024 | URL: https://www.pib.gov.in/pressreleasepage.aspx?PRID=2057454&lang=2&reg=48 | Summary: As a joint statement signed by Modi, the Quad opposed destabilizing actions by force or coercion and reaffirmed peaceful resolution. This supports truthfulness in formal diplomacy, though it is collective and not proof of general personal honesty. | Question IDs: 7B.1, 1B.4, 6B.6
- **Coalition bargaining over funds and cabinet jobs** | Publisher: Reuters via Investing.com | Date: 6 Jun 2024 | URL: https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/modis-appeal-clouded-in-india-election-by-prices-jobs-graft-survey-says-3472931 | Summary: Regional allies demanded funds and cabinet positions as coalition talks began. This is not direct lying, but it is evidence of transactional politics that often accompanies selective truth-telling and public spin. | Question IDs: 7B.1, 6B.9, 6B.10

**Search Gap**
- I did not find a clean, independent 2024 example in the indexed material of Modi lying under oath to Parliament or a court.
- Most negative evidence comes from campaign/public messaging, state information control, and pressure on media, not from documented false testimony in a formal legal setting.
- So the strongest defensible claim is not “proved habitual liar in every arena,” but rather “repeatedly willing to use misleading communal messaging and information control when it served power, while remaining procedurally compliant in some formal diplomatic and electoral settings.”
